ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit दक्षिणायन (dakṣiṇāyana). By surface analysis, दक्षिण (dakṣiṇ, “south”) + अयन (ayan, “movement, path”).

Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *पिल्लअ (pillaa) without cluster simplification. Compare Prakrit पीलुअ (pīlua), पेल्ल (pĕlla), पेल्लग (pĕllaga, “child”), पिल्ह (pilha, “fledgeling”), and Pali पिल्लक (pillaka, “young of animal, child”). Ultimately from Dravidian, whence Malayalam പിള്ള (piḷḷa), Tamil பிள்ளை (piḷḷai), Kannada ಪಿಳ್ಳೆ (piḷḷe), Telugu పిల్ల (pilla). Indo-Aryan cognates include Bengali পিল (pil), Gujarati પીલો (pīlo), Marathi पिल्लू (pillū), Konkani पिल्लू (pillū).
